title: Table gesture heuristics and density heatmap overlays for large virtualized datasets
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and deliver a set of interaction heuristics and visual overlays that help users understand table density and safely manipulate columns in very wide, virtualized tables. This includes a lightweight density heatmap layer, predictive resize handoff rules (mouse, touch, keyboard), and failure-safe behaviors when virtualization prevents accurate measurements.
background: We continue to see support requests and usability regressions for large tables (>200 columns / very wide grids). Users frequently misjudge where content is visually dense, and accidental column drifts happen when resizing across virtualized boundaries. Engineering implemented a partial virtualization shim to reduce DOM cost, but it hides spatial continuity cues. This ticket ties a design proposal to an implementable heuristics spec that balances UX clarity and runtime performance.
goals: Provide an unobtrusive density visualization so users can spot crowded regions and choose density presets
Define deterministic column-resize handoff heuristics across virtualization boundaries for mouse and touch
Ensure keyboard-first behavior for resize and column movement is predictable and accessible
Keep runtime overhead small (<2ms per frame addition, and optional in app settings)
decisions: Introduce a semi-transparent 'density heatmap' overlay rendered by canvas (or GPU layer) to avoid DOM bloat
Predictive handoff: when dragging a column and the next column is not rendered due to virtualization, show a ghost indicator and snap region rather than relying on pixel-perfect hit tests

Expose a compact density dial in the column header menu with three presets: Default, Compact, Compressed; changing presets triggers a server-side suggestion for suggested column widths for certain data types
Keyboard interactions use a two-step mode: focus column header -> press 'R' to enter resize mode -> arrow keys adjust width, Esc cancels, Enter commits
tradeoffs: Canvas overlay reduces DOM work but makes per-cell semantic overlays harder; we'll add accessible text alternatives for screen readers
Predictive handoff may occasionally snap differently than user's muscle memory; to mitigate we show a short animation and allow undo with Cmd/Ctrl+Z
Enabling heatmap by default could add render cost on extremely large tables; default to off for low-powered devices and provide telemetry opt-in
acceptance_criteria: Design spec with annotated behaviors for mouse/touch/keyboard handoff merged into FigJam (link in links)
Prototype demonstrating heatmap overlay on a 10k-row x 500-column synthetic dataset with virtualization toggled
Engineering implementation plan with performance measurements (FPS and CPU delta) and a feature flag for toggling overlay
Usability test (5 participants) with task completion improvement or equivalent reduction in accidental column moves
Accessibility checklist completed: focus state announced, ARIA for density toggle, keyboard resize flow documented
